audit.why: Difficulty 4/10 FAVOURED matches a melee-vs-immobile-soldier-mage lane where Irelia's Bladesurge (600 range, 10/9/8/7/6s, refreshes on Marked or dying targets) turns the wave into gap-closers. Emerald+ win rate is 50.12% over 433 games, which is closer to even than the 8/10 rows suggest, but the direction of the page is right.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 text claimed Vanguard's Edge knocks Azir up. Riot's text for Irelia R is damage + Mark + a slowing wall; there is no knockup. Azir's Emperor's Divide is the knockback in this matchup.
audit.why: A fabricated displacement changes how a player commits at 6.
audit.corrected: R Marks him (refreshing Bladesurge onto a Marked target) and leaves a slowing wall; the knockback belongs to Azir.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shifting Sands' shield was never stated as burst absorption, and no real cooldowns appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Shifting Sands (E) is 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s and both shields and dashes; it is the single window that decides when Irelia may commit. Bladesurge 10/9/8/7/6s, Defiant Dance 20/18/16/14/12s, Vanguard's Edge 125/105/85s, Emperor's Divide 120/105/90s.
audit.corrected: Bait Shifting Sands, then commit inside its 16-22s downtime; Irelia's E is the hard CC in the lane and Azir has no cleanse for it in kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Shifting Sands 22s/16s, Bladesurge 10s, Emperor's Divide 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The title promised one thing and the body explained another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles (passive stacking; wave-as-dashes).

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - W Defiant Dance spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Shifting Sands is down 22s at rank 1 and 16s maxed — his shield and his escape leave together, so step up the second it burns. - Bladesurge is 10s at rank 1 but refunds on a Marked or dying target. - Emperor's Divide is 120s; his wall is not always there.

edits.before: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Shifting Sands shields him through your burst — bait it out, then Q the wave into his chest.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Stacks come off spells hitting anything: Q the wave, land E, and your autos arrive at max attack speed with bonus on-hit already live.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Every low minion is a 600-range Bladesurge target; shove them into his turret and you deleted your own gap-closer for 10s.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Azir wins by keeping soldiers between you two, poking with Conquering Sands, and knocking your dive back with his wall.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry inside soldier range: low minions are free 600-range dashes and your wall cuts the retreat Shifting Sands planned.

edits.before: If Azir opens the score, reset expectations and respect Shifting Sands doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q resets and stay relevant through stacked windows.
edits.after: If Azir opens the score, stop stepping into soldier range without Bladesurge up. Farm the side minions for resets, hold Defiant Dance for Conquering Sands, and re-enter only once his 16-22s Shifting Sands is spent.

edits.before: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions — every one is a dash and the crash is an all-in announcement you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane — no minions, no dashes, no Irelia. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions between you and him — each is a 600-range Bladesurge and the crash is an all-in you control. Worst wave: a shoved lane where his soldiers outrange you and there is nothing left to dash to. Crash timing: crash while Shifting Sands is on cooldown, then take plates or reset — never into a full-mana Azir holding his dash.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Azir's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, hold the wave low in his face: he cannot farm past a live Bladesurge threat, and every recall he takes hands you plates.

edits.before: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, stun the carries, and let the marks ground the peel.
edits.after: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, E-stun the carries, and let R's wall slow whoever tries to peel.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge dashes through his zone control and knocks him up, so level 6 stays in your favour despite his ult
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge Marks him and walls his retreat, refunding Bladesurge, so level 6 stays in your favour despite his ult

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge dashes and knocks up through his soldier zoning, so Emperor's Divide doesn't actually buy him the space he needs to kite you at 6.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge Marks him and leaves a slowing wall behind him, so Emperor's Divide only knocks you back into a lane he still cannot kite you out of at 6.

edits.before: Level 6 doesn't flip anything here. Emperor's Divide is a zone-control ult, not a lockdown tool, and Vanguard's Edge dashes and knocks him up right through the soldier wall he's counting on. Keep initiating within a couple seconds of his soldier landing so he never gets a full combo stacked — your all-in speed beats his ramp-up every time. Roams are close to even since neither side has hard CC to punish a missing laner, so contest based on wave state rather than conceding priority.
edits.after: Level 6 doesn't flip anything here. Emperor's Divide knocks you back rather than locking you down, and Vanguard's Edge answers it: the blades Mark him, Bladesurge refunds onto a Marked target, and you re-close the gap his 120s ult just bought. Keep initiating within a couple seconds of his soldier landing so he never stacks a full rotation — your all-in speed beats his ramp-up. Your E-stun makes your roams the dangerous ones, so take priority and contest on wave state rather than conceding it.

edits.before: Azir's kite gets safer with more soldiers and CDR, but Vanguard's Edge still dashes and knocks up through his zone, and your reset-fueled all-in kills him before he stacks a full poke rotation. Buy MR to shrug off the chip damage and keep closing distance fast instead of standing in soldier range; your win condition stays forcing quick fights, and the numbers back you even into the late game.
edits.after: Azir's kite gets safer with more soldiers and CDR, but Vanguard's Edge Marks whoever it hits at 950 range and refunds Bladesurge, so your reset chain re-closes every gap his wall buys and Emperor's Divide only relocates the fight. Buy MR to shrug off the chip and close distance instead of standing in soldier range; your win condition stays forcing quick fights, and the numbers back you even into the late game.

notes: Irelia's R has no knockup in Riot's text (damage + Mark + slowing wall); three fields asserted one and are corrected. Level chart left untouched: packet levelChart and the page agree (all Irelia), so there is no disagreement to fix — but every row rated 7-8/10 against a 50.12% Emerald+ win rate over 433 games is a tension I did not resolve from the kit alone. tradeBad and loading left as-is; they are voice, not defect.
